title: NO KINGS Mankato
description:
Donald Trump thinks his rule is absolute, but in America, we don’t do “kings.” Since the inauguration, the Trump administration and its enablers have operated as though they have a mandate—but they don’t, and never did. They are going to extremes to empower Trump and enrich themselves, while cutting jobs and services for the rest of us. Now, they’re turning Flag Day into a celebration of Trump.

Join us in Mankato Saturday, June 14, from 11-12:30 pm to say:

We are united against kings.

No using OUR tax dollars to pay for HIS party.

They’ve gone too far: This is bigger than political disagreement. They’ve defied our courts, deported American citizens, disappeared people off the streets, and slashed our services—all while orchestrating a massive giveaway to their billionaire allies. Enough is enough. For anyone who thinks he’s gone too far, this movement is for you.

LOGISTICS

We will rally on the sidewalks along two busy side streets in Mankato, Warren St and South Broad St: north on Broad from Warren to Cherry, and 1-2 blocks east and west of Broad on Warren. 

Based on attendance, we will extend the rally in those 3 directions, following the guidance of rally leaders.

Volunteers will assist participants with logistical information and support on rally sidewalks rather than at a central location.

Please use legal, public parking only. Consider arriving by 10:30 to park and find your place. If able, please use parking ramps and walk. Free municipal ramps include Mankato Place, Civic Center, Second Street, and City Center ramps. The last one is the garage along Riverfront Drive between Cherry and Warren streets.

Bring a sign or two, water, cash for emergencies, and weather-appropriate clothing. The nearest bathrooms are a couple of blocks away, so be prepared for that too.

SAFETY

A core principle behind all NO KINGS events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values, and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events. We ask participants to obey traffic and other laws and be mindful of pedestrians using the sidewalks. There will be a police presence at the event but we will rely on our own peacekeepers, volunteers, and you to assist with de-escalation. If asked by leaders or police to disperse, please do so at once.

This event is co-sponsored by Indivisible St. Peter/Greater Mankato and ACLU MN and COPAL MN. Thank you so much for standing with us!

title: NO KINGS
description:
Let’s unite to defend our Constitution and push back against the troubling direction our country is heading!

We reject efforts to normalize displays of power meant to intimidate rather than inspire. Instead, we stand for a democracy rooted in compassion, transparency, and collective action. No Kings means no to fascism, no to fear, and yes to a future where people come before politics.

Right now, Congress is working on a bill that would take healthcare away from millions of people but still give billionaires more tax breaks. It’s a clear example of unfair priorities that hurt everyday families while helping the richest get richer.

We believe healthcare is a human right. We believe in a democracy that serves the people, not the powerful. And we believe it’s our responsibility to rise up and defend those principles.

Please bring a non-perishable food item to support our local food pantry—because community care and mutual aid are acts of resistance!

Join us in solidarity. Together, we’ll show that we will not be silenced, we will not be intimidated, and we will never stop fighting for justice and dignity for all!

title: Virtual Town Hall: Attacks on the Rule of Law
description:
Join Attorneys General Kathy Jennings of Delaware, Kwame Raoul of
Illinois, Matt Platkin of New Jersey, and Brian Schwalb of the District of
Columbia, Skye Perryman, President & CEO of Democracy Forward, and
Cecillia Wang, National Legal Director of ACLU, for a national call to
discuss the unprecedented assault on the rule of law by the Trump
administration. This call will focus on the Trump administration’s efforts
to undermine the practice of law and law firms, the courts, and the justice
system, and detail how Attorneys General and legal organizations are
successfully fighting back.

State Attorneys General alongside key legal organizations have led the
fight against the worst abuses of the Trump Administration. Since
Inauguration Day, Attorneys General have brought more than 30 lawsuits
and legal actions, Democracy Forward has brought more than 70 lawsuits
and legal actions, and the ACLU has brought more than 50 lawsuits and
more than 100 legal actions — and all have won key injunctions.

title: Debrief & Strategy Call
description:
Join Vote Forward Executive Director Yasmin Radjy and Senior Director of Data & Research Emily Wasserman as we debrief the results of our 2024 letter writing campaigns and share strategies for what comes next.

Since the 2024 election, Vote Forward has engaged in rigorous analysis and deep reflection to inform our response to this challenging moment. We’re now ready to debut the results transparently and introduce our next steps. 

Every cycle, Vote Forward runs numerous RCT (randomized controlled trials) to test the effectiveness of our voter turnout programs. Then, in our continued pursuit of innovation and commitment to transparency, we share our learnings with our volunteers and supporters, peer organizations, and the public. 

We know there’s too much at stake to keep doing the same old thing—and figuring out what works in our new political, media, and cultural landscape requires intense evidence-driven experimentation and testing. This is the time for creativity, innovation, and big bets to win the elections that will matter most to the future of democracy.

By embracing what the Vote Forward community does best—developing and testing smart voter contact strategies powered by volunteers and sharing our learnings—we can be part of the solution. RSVP for the call Monday, June 9th at 8pm ET/ 5pm PT.

title: NCDC Supports Juneteenth at Meyer Amphitheater
description:
Join the clubs and caucuses of the PBC Democratic Executive Committee as we celebrate Juneteenth on 6/22/25 from 5-10.  Volunteer to help recruit leaders, register voters, and talk about Democratic Values. 

Juneteenth commemorates the emancipation of enslaved African Americans in Texas on June 19, 1865, marking the end of slavery in the United States. 
It's a time for reflection, remembrance, and celebrating the progress towards freedom and equality, as well as recognizing that the fight for justice and equity continues. 

Juneteenth, also known as "Freedom Day" or "Emancipation Day," commemorates the arrival of Union soldiers in Galveston, Texas, announcing that enslaved people were free, two years after the Emancipation Proclamation was issued. 

Juneteenth celebrations often include prayer services, speeches, educational events, and community gatherings with food, music, and dancing. 

While Juneteenth originated in Texas, it's now celebrated across the United States and even internationally as a reminder of the ongoing struggle for freedom and equality. 

Juneteenth is a time to acknowledge the progress made while also recognizing that the fight for true equality continues, including issues like voter suppression and racial justice. 

Many see Juneteenth as a connection to other emancipation celebrations across the African diaspora, highlighting a shared history of striving for freedom and independence.

description:
Join us for another Roadside Rally Against Fascism down in Bellmawr at the corner of Black Horse Pike and E Browning Road.

This is a nonviolent demonstration, so please attend with safety and de-escalation in mind. We do not expect any counterprotestors, but we can never be 100% sure. Do your best to minimize engagement with hecklers, and don't be too shy to smile and wave at our supporters!

See you out there!

title: June Stop Voter Suppression Town Hall
description:
Anti-voter lawmakers and supporters of the SAVE Act and HJR B have introduced two petition drives that would make it harder for Michiganders to exercise their right to vote by introducing oppressive voter registration requirements.

Breakout discussions on chapters that spoke to us most

Next steps . . . A plan to implement what we have learned from Brooks in our own lives

title: Friday Rally to Protect Democracy in Honor of Our Veterans in Mentor
description:
Come on over to Eleanor Garfield Park in Mentor Friday from 10-11:30am. 

We rally every Friday, but this week's event will be in honor of our veterans.    

June 6th marks the 81st anniversary of D-Day.  

Veterans are planning a massive rally in Washington, D.C., and elsewhere on June 6 to protest cuts at the Department of Veterans Affairs and call for the protection of veterans' benefits and jobs, which are being hurt by the Trump administration's efforts to reduce the size of the federal government.

We will gather in solidarity with veterans.  We will stand along Mentor Avenue with signs and flags. We will peacefully show that we object to the insidious cuts to vital federal programs and employees.

District 14 members will have the opportunity to fill out comment sheets for Congressman Dave Joyce.

Bring signs, friends, and family. Bring family-friendly signs.

We will be donating food to the Geauga County Veteran's Food Pantry.  Please check their website for items they need:

www.geaugacountyveteranfoodpantry.com

Donating is optional.

Please park in the lower lot if you are able to make the walk up to the event site. Please keep the spaces in the upper lot open for those who need a shorter walk.

This event is sponsored by Ohio District 14 Partners in collaboration with the pro-democracy groups in Ohio's District 14.

Note—this event was formerly titled ‘Where’s Congressman Joyce.” Though the title has changed, we still wonder where he is, and why he is not answering our specific concerns.

title: Unite for Veterans - INW Meetup onsite | Indivisible NOVA West
description:
On June 6th, join thousands of veterans, military families, and their allies on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., for the Unite for Veterans, Unite for America Rally hosted by the AFL-CIO.  Indivisible NOVA West members will carpool and/or take Metro, and meet up and join allies Common Defense and WOFA onsite. Details provided to attendees

America made a promise to its veterans. It's a promise we intend to keep.

We are coming together to defend the benefits, jobs, and dignity that every generation of veterans has earned through sacrifice.

Veteran jobs, healthcare, and essential VA services are under attack. We will not stand by.

Why We Rally Veterans and military family members are being fired by the thousands from federal jobs. Our healthcare is being gutted. Our benefits are under siege.

This isn't the first time veterans have had to fight for what was promised. From the Bonus Army of 1932 to the battles for the GI Bill and Agent Orange care, veterans have always led the charge for justice.

Now, it's our turn.

We rally to:

-Defend veteran and military family member employment in the federal workforce

-Stop the privatization and weakening of the Department of Veterans Affairs

-Hold political leaders accountable for policies that harm veterans and their families
